title: NaN MultiIndex column labels wrap around to last level in to_excel
answers: Why does DataFrame.to_excel write NaN MultiIndex column labels as the last value of that level?
How to prevent NaN column labels in MultiIndex from writing incorrect values in to_excel?
Why does Index.take wrap around negative -1 codes when formatting MultiIndex levels in Excel?
How are missing or NaN MultiIndex header values handled in ExcelFormatter?
body:
Symptom: Exporting a DataFrame with MultiIndex columns containing NaN labels via `to_excel` writes the NaN label as the last value of that level instead of an empty cell.
Root cause: `pandas/io/formats/excel.py:ExcelFormatter._format_header_mi` calls `levels.take(level_codes)` without `allow_fill=True`, causing the `-1` code for NaN to wrap around to the last element.
Fix pattern: Pass `allow_fill=True` to `levels.take(level_codes, allow_fill=True)` so that `-1` sentinel codes are filled with NaN instead of wrapping around.
Constraints: Applies when taking MultiIndex level values using `codes` that may contain `-1` for missing/NaN values; not required if codes are guaranteed non-negative.
applies: Formatting MultiIndex column headers with NaN or missing labels in DataFrame.to_excel
